title: Rent Control Act - Security Deposit Limit
content: Under the Rent Control Act, landlords typically cannot demand security deposit exceeding 2-3 months' rent. In some jurisdictions like Delhi, the maximum security deposit is equivalent to one month's rent for residential properties. Excessive deposits may be challenged in rent control courts.

title: Model Tenancy Act - Rent Increase Guidelines
content: As per the Model Tenancy Act (2021), landlords can increase rent by a maximum of 10% per year or as mutually agreed in the rental agreement. Any rent hike must be preceded by a 3-month notice period. Rent cannot be increased during the fixed term unless explicitly stated in the agreement.

title: Landlord Maintenance Responsibilities
content: Landlords are responsible for major structural repairs, electrical wiring, plumbing, and sanitary fittings. Routine maintenance charges (if included in rent) cannot exceed 10% of the monthly rent. Tenants are responsible for minor day-to-day repairs and damages caused by negligence.

title: Model Tenancy Act - Notice Period Requirements
content: For month-to-month tenancies, either party must give at least one month's notice before vacating. For fixed-term leases, early termination requires mutual consent or may attract penalty equivalent to 1-2 months' rent unless justified by breach of contract by the other party.

title: Security Deposit Refund Timeline
content: Upon termination of tenancy, the security deposit must be refunded within 30 days after the tenant vacates the premises and hands over possession. Deductions can only be made for unpaid rent, damages beyond normal wear and tear, or pending utility bills. Itemized deduction statement must be provided.

title: Mandatory Rent Receipt and TDS
content: Landlords are required to provide rent receipts to tenants. If annual rent exceeds Rs. 2.5 lakhs, tenants are liable to deduct TDS @ 10% under Section 194-IB of Income Tax Act. Landlord must provide PAN details to tenant for TDS compliance.

title: Lock-in Period in Lease Agreements
content: A lock-in period of minimum 6 months to maximum 3 years is enforceable. During lock-in, neither party can terminate without paying/forfeiting penalty (usually 1-3 months' rent). Lock-in protects both parties from premature termination.

title: Subletting and Assignment Restrictions
content: Tenants cannot sublet, assign, or part with possession without prior written consent of the landlord. Unauthorized subletting is grounds for eviction. However, landlords cannot unreasonably withhold consent unless the agreement explicitly prohibits subletting.

title: Utility Bills Payment Responsibility
content: Unless explicitly agreed, tenants are responsible for electricity, water, gas, and maintenance charges. If maintenance charges are included in rent, they cannot exceed actual society maintenance bills plus maximum 15% administrative charge.

title: Jurisdiction for Rental Disputes
content: All rental disputes fall under the jurisdiction of the courts where the property is situated. Parties can include arbitration clauses but cannot oust jurisdiction of courts completely. Consumer forums can entertain disputes relating to deficiency in service by landlords.
applicable_law: Civil Procedure Code & Consumer Protection Act

title: Interest on Security Deposit
content: Security deposits are generally interest-free in residential tenancies. However, some states like Maharashtra mandate that landlords pay interest on security deposits above Rs. 50,000 at the rate of 0.5% per annum if the deposit is held for more than 12 months.

title: Painting and Repair Charges at Vacancy
content: Normal wear and tear cannot be charged to the tenant. Painting charges at the time of vacating can be recovered if excessive damage is proven (beyond normal 5-year repaint cycle). Landlord must provide quotes/invoices for any deductions claimed from security deposit.

title: Occupancy Limits and Family Definition
content: Standard occupancy limits are typically 2 persons per bedroom plus one additional occupant (e.g., family of 3 for a 2BHK). Landlords cannot unreasonably restrict immediate family members (spouse, children, parents) from occupying, but can limit unrelated occupants.

title: Valid Grounds for Tenant Eviction
content: Valid eviction grounds include: non-payment of rent for 2+ consecutive months, unauthorized subletting, causing damage to property, use for illegal activities, nuisance to neighbors, violation of lease terms, and landlord's bonafide need for self-occupancy (with proper notice and compensation in some jurisdictions).

title: Mandatory Rent Receipt Under GST
content: For GST purposes, if rent exceeds Rs. 500 per transaction, landlords registered under GST must provide a rent receipt. Unregistered landlords below threshold are exempt but still recommended to issue receipts for tenant records.
